report.summary: Reviewed drift.py chunk 6 (lines 1401-end): drift item construction, acceptance handling, refresh, main. Claims mostly kept; several uncheckable due to cross-chunk references.
risks: drift.py:1401 | medium | NEW_DARK_SWITCH item uses result.sites.get('dark-switch:' + name, '?') and 'introduced in no document' — if such a switch is actually documented elsewhere, the claim is wrong; needs cross-check of sites dictionary and document scan.
drift.py:1421 | medium | old_ignore non-dict fallback to {"env":"","file":""} — if snapshot has a non-dict ignore, the comparison may be misleading; needs verification of actual snapshot format.
drift.py:1449 | high | ACCEPTABLE_KINDS referenced but not defined in this chunk — if it excludes a kind that should be acceptable, acceptances would not match; needs cross-check.
drift.py:1449 | medium | by_key groups only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS items; items of other kinds never get accepted, even if an acceptance targets them — potential silent staleness.
drift.py:1487 | medium | ok = not any(i.blocking for i in items) — if blocking is None or truthy non-bool, logic may be off; needs definition of DriftItem.blocking.

drift.py:1510 | medium | refresh carries acceptances verbatim from old snapshot — if old snapshot has invalid acceptances, they are carried forward without validation; claim 'never quietly drop' kept but validity not rechecked.
drift.py:1544 | medium | main --init uses check(write_missing=True) but check may not write missing snapshot in all cases; needs cross-check of check implementation.

drift.py:1565 | medium | main --init returns 0 even if report.ok is False (it prints report and returns 0); if check returns a report with ok=False on first run, this would be a green exit on a failing report; needs cross-check.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: drift item construction for dark switches, unparsable modules, doc drift, ignore config, acceptance application, and CLI entry points.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Re-baselines snapshot: scans, loads old snapshot, parses acceptances, writes new snapshot with acceptances carried forward.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses args, builds index, handles --refresh, --init, and check; exits with code based on report.

claims.text: A run that looks at less of the tree than the baseline did cannot be compared with it, and a green result from one must never be indistinguishable from a green result from the other
claims.why: The code compares old_ignore and new_ignore and emits an IGNORE_DRIFT item when they differ, making the run non-green.

claims.text: Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match. An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: by_key only collects items whose kind is in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS; acceptances only match those items. If an item is now reachable and its kind is acceptable, the acceptance matches it and marks it accepted, which is the intended behavior.

claims.text: An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: The code matches acceptances against current items; if an item is now present and acceptable, the acceptance matches it and marks it accepted, not stale. If it were not present, it would go stale.

claims.text: Refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: refresh parses acceptances from the old snapshot and passes them verbatim to write_snapshot, so they are carried forward.

claims.text: CI gate, not a pre-commit hook: it parses the whole tree and takes seconds.
claims.why: The CLI runs check which scans the whole tree; no pre-commit hook behavior is present.

claims.text: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run
claims.why: In main, --init only writes if snap.is_file() is false; otherwise it returns 1. For normal check, if snapshot missing, check likely returns first_run=True and main returns 1 (fail closed).

claims.text: Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: refresh parses acceptances from old snapshot and passes them to write_snapshot unchanged.

claims.text: The baseline was taken under {old_ignore}. A run that looks at less of the tree than the baseline did cannot be compared with it, and a green result from one must never be indistinguishable from a green result from the other
claims.why: The code emits an IGNORE_DRIFT item when ignore configs differ, which makes the report non-green (assuming blocking kind).

claims.text: Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was.
claims.why: old_ignore is defaulted to {"env":"","file":""} when not a dict, so absence is treated as empty ignore, not as a different state; comparison still detects changes.

claims.text: Fail CLOSED, matching `daedalus map --check`. This used to write the baseline and exit 0, which made `rm docs/architecture-state.json` a green run through a door reach.py itself classifies as an entry point.
claims.why: When report.first_run is true, main returns 1, failing closed.

claims.text: An ABSENT key reads as "nothing was excluded", not as "do not check".
claims.why: old_ignore is set to {"env":"","file":""} when not a dict, which represents no exclusions.

claims.text: A green result from one must never be indistinguishable from a green result from the other
claims.why: The IGNORE_DRIFT item is added when ignore configs differ, so the report is not green in that case (assuming blocking kind).

claims.text: An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: The code matches acceptances against current items; if an item is now present and acceptable, the acceptance matches it and marks it accepted, not stale. If it were not present, it would go stale.
When an acceptance is expired, the note states that the reason outlived its horizon.
